data.description: The final fare was $16.50 but the upfront quote was $12.00 and nobody told me about surge. When I asked the driver about it he shouted at me, locked the doors and threatened me, saying I would not get out of the car until I paid. I felt unsafe and scared. I want the $4.50 difference back.

data.content: Hi, I'm at the taxi stand outside Bugis Junction near the fountain.
OK, I see you. Pulling up now, white Prius.
The fare is $16.50, why? The quote was $12. Please open the door, I want to get out.
Pay the full fare first or I will not let you out of this car. Do not test me.

Platform surge record: multipliers, activation time, rider notification.

json.account_summary: The rider says the final fare was $16.50 against an upfront quote of $12.00, that nobody told the rider about surge, and that the difference of $4.50 is in dispute [E-TKT-01]. The record shows a quote of $12.00, an actual fare of $16.50, and a surge change from 1.0x to 1.5x, with the platform surge record showing no rider notification [E-TRP-01] [E-PAY-01] [E-SRG-01]. The rider says that when the rider asked the driver about the fare, the driver shouted, locked the doors and threatened that the rider would not get out until the fare was paid, and that the rider felt unsafe and scared [E-TKT-01]. The chat record shows a rider message at 21:18:30 asking about the fare and asking for the door to be opened, followed by a driver message at 21:18:50 saying the rider must pay the full fare first or the driver will not let the rider out, and "Do not test me" [E-CHT-03] [E-CHT-04]. The chat does not record any shouting or door locking, and GPS shows the vehicle stopped at 21:18:00 [E-GPS-07]. Under Section 5.2 this summary only presents the rider's account and the records, and the matter is for a human reviewer.

The shouting and door locking are described only in the rider's statement, and no driver account is in the file [E-TKT-01]. Because the file contains safety indicators, Section 5.2 applies and this file is prepared for a human reviewer, with no ruling, fault finding or recommendation. The contested $4.50 surge charge is recorded as a secondary claim, with no view on it.

data.description: The final fare was $16.50 but the upfront quote was $12.00 and nobody told me about surge. When I asked the driver about it he shouted at me, locked the doors and threatened me, saying I would not get out of the car until I paid. I felt unsafe and scared. I want the $4.50 difference back.

data.content: Hi, I'm at the taxi stand outside Bugis Junction near the fountain.
OK, I see you. Pulling up now, white Prius.
The fare is $16.50, why? The quote was $12. Please open the door, I want to get out.
Pay the full fare first or I will not let you out of this car. Do not test me.

evidence.summary: Fare breakdown: quote, actual fare, excess and surge lines (platform record).
Platform surge record: multipliers, activation time, rider notification.

rider_advocate_brief.account_summary: The rider says the final fare was $16.50 against an upfront quote of $12.00, that nobody told the rider about surge, and that the difference of $4.50 is in dispute [E-TKT-01]. The record shows a quote of $12.00, an actual fare of $16.50, and a surge change from 1.0x to 1.5x, with the platform surge record showing no rider notification [E-TRP-01] [E-PAY-01] [E-SRG-01]. The rider says that when the rider asked the driver about the fare, the driver shouted, locked the doors and threatened that the rider would not get out until the fare was paid, and that the rider felt unsafe and scared [E-TKT-01]. [removed: a safety case file proposes no ruling, finding of fault or recommendation (policy v2.1 Section 5.2)] The chat does not record any shouting or door locking, and GPS shows the vehicle stopped at 21:18:00 [E-GPS-07]. Under Section 5.2 this summary only presents the rider's account and the records, and the matter is for a human reviewer.
